labels.label: cor:property_defined_cycles_gcd
labels.notes: Unmarked, which is correct. tools/ledger.py:247's regex (``**`label`**``) matches nothing anywhere in the file. The SCOPE bullets that open with a backticked label in bold (l.64, l.105, l.113) do not close the bold right after the backtick, and they start past character 4000 (l.64 is at character 4578). The row is partial. Lean ≥ paper, hypothesis by hypothesis, under the disclosed readings. (1) 𝒫 is any P : ℤ → ℕ → Prop on pairs (x, n) with n ≥ 1 and Tⁿx = x. A property of orbits embeds as P'(x, n) := n minimal ∧ 𝒫(orbit). Its hypothesis is then the paper's, because p_n and the GCD are constant along an orbit. (2) « ≪ » is read as ∃ ε > 0, ∃ C, ∀ pairs, with C uniform in Γ. That is the standard Vinogradov reading. The closer's remark about a Γ-dependent C is right. Such a hypothesis holds for every pair with C := |2^p − 3ⁿ| / 2^{p(1−ε)}, which a probe checked. The corollary would then claim finiteness for P = True, which is false for pairs: (1, k), k ≥ 1. For orbits it would be an open problem, and the REPORT limits its claim to pairs. The 'eventually' variant reduces to this one through citedSteps_finite_of_le, as stated. (3) |Γ| is read as p_n. The proof's couples (|Γ|, n) exclude |Γ| = n. That reading would also be covered, since n ≤ p_n makes the p_n hypothesis the weaker one. (4) The GCD comes in two readings, Aun (printed) and AunAlt (OQ-43), each under ∃ α, c. The existential is harmless: the GCD over a period is shift-invariant, and citedSteps_gcd_dvd shows it is the GCD over ℤ. The …_mr and …_matveev forms assume only |2^{p_n} − 3ⁿ| ≤ C 2^{p_n(1−ε)}, which is weaker by citedSteps_abs_le_gcd. (5) The conclusion is that the set of pairs is finite, which also bounds the orbits. (6) From CitedStepsMR the corollary holds over all of ℤ. From CitedStepsMatveev it holds on positive cycles only, which is disclosed and is Finding 1. (7) The effective clause is a disclosed reading: an explicit B(C, ε) bounds p_n, and every 𝒫-cycle lies in the computable Finset citedStepsCandidates ⌊B⌋₊. CitedStepsMR (l.152) is theo:mr (l.145–148) as printed: a, b ∈ ℤ, δ ∈ ℝ with δ ≥ 1, and e^{−a/δ} written as exp(−a/δ). CitedStepsMatveev (l.145) is theo:matveev (l.156–159) as printed: a, b ∈ ℕ* with 2^a > 3^b, and e^d a^d written as exp(d)·a^d, with d = 3500000 = 3.5·10⁶ exactly. Both are defs taken as explicit hypotheses, not axioms. Neither contains the corollary. Neither is false, as far as the literature goes. For theo:mr, a counterexample would need a ≥ 2^{800} log(3)^{25} δ^{25} and |a log 2 − b log 3| ≤ exp(−≈4.7·10⁹·a^{0.96}). Laurent's two-logarithm bound, log|Λ| ≥ −c(log a)² with c ≈ 19, excludes that. For theo:matveev, the range a ≤ d is proved (citedStepsMatveev_of_le). Above it the inequality follows from effective lower bounds of the form |Λ| ≥ a^{−O(1)}, and d is enormous by comparison. Non-vacuity at real cycles is proved. With P = two descents, (−17, 7) lies in the finite set (from theo:mr). With P = one descent, (1, 1) lies in it (from theo:matveev). Both hypotheses h hold, by the strict twoDesc_corollary_hyp and steiner_corollary_hypothesis. citedStepsCandidates contains (1, 1), (−1, 1), (−5, 2) and (−17, 7) by decide. citedSteps_twoDescMatveev_of_matveev and …_of_mr discharge the strict TwoDescMatveev B from either cited Prop, at an explicit B.

labels.label: prop:proposition
labels.notes: Unmarked, which is correct. The row is partial. prop_proposition_of_check (l.979) is the printed statement with exactly one added hypothesis, CitedStepsCheck, which is disclosed. Its parts: x ∈ ℤ; 0 < n; Tⁿx = x; 1000 < |x|; α n ≤ #{i ∈ Icc 1 n | a i x = 1}; and the conjunct 0.415037499 < α, with α = 2 − logb 2 3 − 1/10^{10}. The count uses the a_i of l.62. citedStepsOnes_eq_range shows it equals the count in the convention of l.71 on every cycle, so the statement is the same under both readings of OQ-63 (b). CitedStepsCheck (l.159) is l.201's first clause: every odd 0 < y < 10^{10} reaches 1 under T. It is true, since Collatz has been verified far beyond 10^{10}. CitedStepsCycleCheck (l.164) is not assumed separately. It is proved from the check by citedStepsCycleCheck_of_check (l.946), which goes through cycle_avoids_neg_third for oddness and citedSteps_eq_one_of_iterate. The theorems that take it (prop_proposition_ne_one, …_of_cycleCheck) therefore assume less. Neither Prop contains the conclusion, which still needs Syracuse.bounds and p_n ≥ a + 2(n − a). prop_proposition_neg (l.870) is unconditional. Its only hypotheses are x < 0, 0 < n and Tⁿx = x: no cited Prop and no |x| > 1000. It concludes (2 − log₂3)n < count and αn < count. Its axioms are standard. The counts, recomputed in Python from T, are 1 at −1 (n = 1), 1 at −5 and 1 at −7 (n = 2), and 5 at −17 (n = 7, a = (1,1,1,2,1,1,4), p₇ = 11). Each exceeds αn ≈ 0.415, 0.830, 0.830, 2.905. The count at (1) is 0, which confirms prop_proposition_unbounded_false. The arithmetic was checked exactly. 3^{79335} < 2^{125743} holds. 125743/79335 is a convergent of log₂3, the next after 50508/31867, and lies above it by 6.66·10^{−11}. So α ≥ 2 − 125743/79335 − 10^{−10} = 0.4150374991122… > 0.415037499, a margin of 1.12·10^{−10} at the kernel's rational bound. The true margin of α is 1.788·10^{−10}, which the SCOPE gives as about 1.8·10^{−10}.

findings.what: The question says « The step holds with either base ». That is true of the algebra of l.202–204, but not of the closing estimate the proof leaves implicit, log(1 + 1/|x|) < 10^{−10} at |x| > 10^{10}. That estimate holds for the natural log. For log₂ with the printed 1/|x| it fails: log₂(1 + 10^{−10}) ≈ 1.4427·10^{−10} > 10^{−10}. For 10^{10} < |x| < 1.44·10^{10}, the chain then gives a/n ≥ 0.41503749913…, which is below α = 0.41503749917…. With log₂, the step closes only through the true form's 1/(3 min), and that is what the Lean uses: prop_proposition_pos_of_ge, log₂(1 + 1/(3·10^{10})) ≈ 4.8·10^{−11}. Finding 4's « Both quantities are below 10^{−10} » is right only if the two quantities are ln(1 + 1/|x|) and log₂(1 + 1/(3 min)), which the text does not say. The Lean and the conclusion are unaffected.
findings.fix: In REPORT question 3, write: « The algebra of l.202–204 holds with either base. The closing bound log(1 + 1/|x|) < 10^{−10} at |x| > 10^{10} holds for the natural log. For log₂ it needs the true cor:bounds' 1/(3 min), since log₂(1 + 10^{−10}) ≈ 1.44·10^{−10}. » In SCOPE Finding 4, name the two quantities: ln(1 + 1/|x|) and log₂(1 + 1/(3 min)).

findings.what: There are two wording slips in the « effective » finding, which would go to the author. First, « elementary for a < 2^775 …, so the bound it gives on |Γ| exceeds 2^800 » is a non sequitur. The bound exceeds 2^800 because citedStepsBoundMR contains the term 2^{800} log(3)^{25} δ^{25} ≥ 10.5·2^{800}. The elementary range shows something else: no bound drawn from theo:mr can lie below 2^{775}. Second, « a finite computation that cannot be carried out » is true of the enumeration of l.167, where ⟦1, B⟧ⁿ has B ≈ 10^{278} from theo:mr and ≈ 10^{2.69·10^7} from theo:matveev at (C = 2, ε₀ ≈ 0.104), as recomputed. Unqualified, it reads as a claim about every method. The finding itself is correct.
findings.fix: Write: « the bound it gives exceeds 2^800 (it contains 2^800 log(3)^25 δ^25), and no bound from theo:mr can be below 2^775, where its conclusion is elementary ». Also write: « cannot be carried out by the enumeration of l.167 ».

findings.what: CitedStepsMatveev and NoCircuitMatveev state the same thing. CitedStepsMatveev is theo:matveev at the printed d. NoCircuitMatveev C is the same inequality with the constant as a parameter, written (e·P)^C in rpow. A probe checked CitedStepsMatveev ↔ NoCircuitMatveev (3500000 : ℝ) in Lean, by Real.rpow_natCast, mul_pow and Real.exp_nat_mul. NoCircuitMatveev is monotone in C, so CitedStepsMatveev implies NoCircuitMatveev C for every C ≥ d, including NoCircuit's C ≈ 3.6·10⁸ of l.241. NoCircuitMatveevAbs C, the both-sign display of l.240, is a different and stronger statement. Neither should be dropped before T-syr-cited rules. NoCircuit needs the parameter (l.241 has a different constant), and CitedStepsMatveev is the row as printed. Without a bridge, though, the ruling has two names to discharge for one cited theorem. There is no name clash.
findings.fix: At graduation, add one bridge lemma in namespace Syracuse, e.g. `citedStepsMatveev_iff : CitedStepsMatveev ↔ NoCircuitMatveev citedStepsD`, or `NoCircuitMatveev C` for every C ≥ citedStepsD. Alternatively, define CitedStepsMatveev as NoCircuitMatveev citedStepsD. Either way T-syr-cited discharges a single Prop.

summary: Checked: the build under -DwarningAsError=true; the grep for sorry, native_decide, axiom and set_option; #print axioms on all 64 declarations; re-elaboration after `import Syracuse`, alone and joined with NoCircuit.lean's body; the scope; the docstring contract (title, unbolded labels with lines, verbatim quotes, checklist, SCOPE, provenance); the fidelity of the four hypothesis Props to l.145–148, l.156–159 and l.201; and Lean ≥ paper for both rows. Recomputed in exact arithmetic: 3^79335 < 2^125743 and the α bound; the counts at −1, −5, −7, −17 and 1; the GCDs at −17 (AunAlt 2363…12649, GCD 139; Aun 6950…37808, GCD 278; |2^11 − 3^7| = 139); and the bounds' orders of magnitude. All six findings in the REPORT about the paper are true. The three minor items are wording, plus one bridge lemma, all applicable at graduation.
